title: Momentum SDK: Rapid-deploy cheatsheet and prompt playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
This note is a compact, tactical playbook for getting a small team from zero to a running sample integration with the Redwood SDK in ~15–45 minutes. Focus is on momentum: minimal friction, clear rollback points, and a tiny set of prompt presets to validate output quality quickly.

Audience
- New integrator (engineer or product proto lead) who needs a demo or POC fast.
- Solutions engineers running quick customer pilots.

What this doc is not
- Not a full SDK reference. Not exhaustive platform security guidance. Those live in doc refs (links above).

Top-line flow (15 / 45 minute variants)
- 15-minute path (demo-ready):
  1) Install official SDK (npm/pip) and set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var.
  2) Run the sample app: yarn start or python -m momentum_sample.
  3) Swap model in config to a small-latency variant (e.g., redwood-light-3b).
  4) Run 3 warmup requests, then one longer prompt (<= 256 tokens) for demo.
  5) Check Console -> Requests for latency/cost. If > SLO, switch to batching=false or smaller model.
- 45-minute path (validation + telemetry): follow 15-minute path, then:
  6) Wire basic telemetry: enable request_id span and token sampling (see telemetry knobs below).
  7) Add 3 prompt permutations from the Prompt Presets section and compare outputs.
  8) Commit a small feature flag in the sample to flip back to host default on failure.

Quick commands (copy-paste)
- Install: npm i @redwood/sdk OR pip install redwood-sdk
- Start (node): REDWOOD_API_KEY=... node examples/demo.js
- Smoke test: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-light-3b","input":"Hello"}' | jq
- Rollback: git checkout -- examples/config.json && yarn start

Prompt Presets (fast quality checks)
- Preset: Summarize-1 (brevity check)
  "instruction": "Summarize the following paragraph in one sentence, preserve the core fact."
  Use: checks clarity of concise output; expect <= 30 tokens.
- Preset: Expand-2 (detail check)
  "instruction": "Expand the following note into 3 bullet points that an engineer can action."
  Use: verifies output structure and instructions.
- Preset: Safety-quick (hallucination sniff)
  "instruction": "List any factual claims in the text and mark whether they need verification."
  Use: quick sniff for hallucination-prone prompts.

Telemetry knobs (minimal and useful)
- enable_request_id = true (propagate across client + backend)
- sample_tokens = 0.01 (1% heavy sampling for human review)
- log_prompt_length_buckets = [0-64,65-256,257-1024]
- tag_route = "dev-onramp" (important for Console filters)
Notes: keep sampling low in demo to avoid cost, but high enough to catch formatting regressions.

Failure map (fast triage)
- Symptom: very high latency (> SLO)
  Triage: confirm model variant, CPU/GPU mismatch, batching enabled accidentally.
  Quick fix: switch to redwood-light-* or set max_tokens lower.
- Symptom: output is terse / truncated
  Triage: check max_tokens, streaming chunking in client.
  Quick fix: bump max_tokens or switch to non-streaming mode for deterministic checks.
- Symptom: hallucinations/incorrect claims
  Triage: run Safety-quick preset, check system prompt, verify context sources.
  Quick fix: add instruction anchor (e.g., "Only use the facts contained in the input:"), add citation mode.

Runbook: 3-step rollback pattern
1) Stop demo traffic (flip feature flag or remove route in Console).
2) Revert config file + pin known-good model: examples/config.json -> model: redwood-stable-1.
3) Relaunch and run Summarize-1 preset. If still bad, escalate to eng-runtime on Slack #serving-runtime with request_id and short transcript.

UX tips for demos
- Keep one small prompt that shows capability + one that tests edge cases (formats, lists).
- Show telemetry briefly: token cost and latency mid-demo to highlight economics.
- Prepare a canned fallback: "If the model is slow, we'll switch to the lightweight mode and continue" (practice the switch).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Consolidate these presets into the SDK as named validators (api: sdk.validatePreset('summarize-1')).
- Need a tiny UI snippet for demoable model switch in the example app.
- Add a short script to automatically capture 3 runs and produce a diff report.

Links and references
- Linear: DEVEXP-412 (onramp sprint)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/318 (sample app changes)
- Slack thread: #devexp-onboarding (search for "momentum playbook")

Scratchpad and quick scribbles
- If integration target is mobile, pre-warm with one long request to populate token cache.
- For enterprise pilot, add a note: "Ask customer for expected peak RPS and critical latency" before selecting Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Consider a 1-page "demo script" separate doc that maps prompts to expected token counts and fallback steps.

End of draft — feedback welcome.
